# [Standard Access Walkthrough, a Step by Step Guide](https://community.pinterest.biz/t/standard-access-walkthrough-a-step-by-step-guide/52518)

This post is the second in a series on getting up and running on Pinterest. The first article discusses getting Trial Access can be found [here](https://community.pinterest.biz/t/getting-started-with-your-pinterest-developer-app-trial-access/52222/2). For more information on access levels, visit our dev documentation [here.](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/)

Once you have received Trial access for your Pinterest app, you can begin configuring, testing, and preparing your application for a Standard access request.

Standard access is intended for production-ready integrations. Before you apply, make sure your app works as expected, follows Pinterest’s Developer Guidelines, and clearly demonstrates value for users.

## **1. Configure your redirect URI**

Start by opening My apps, selecting Manage for the app you want to upgrade, and navigating to the Configure tab. Add the redirect URI your application uses for Pinterest authentication.

This is one of the most important parts of your setup. The redirect_uri included in your OAuth authorization request must be an exact match to one of the redirect URIs configured in your app profile.

Check each element carefully:

- Protocol: http and https are different, either is fine but make sure you’re using these consistently.
- Domain: Confirm the domain and subdomain match exactly.
- Path: Include the complete callback path.
- Trailing slash: /callback and /callback/ are not the same, either is fine but make sure you’re using these consistently.
- Formatting: Verify ports, capitalization, query parameters, and other URL details.

For example, if your app profile includes:

- [https://example.com/auth/pinterest/callback](https://example.com/auth/pinterest/callback)

These alternatives may result in an error:

- htt***p***://example.com/auth/pinterest/callback <— does not have “s” on the http
- [https://example.com/auth/pinterest/callback/](https://example.com/auth/pinterest/callback/) <— does not match the trailing slash in the original URL
- https://**www**.example.com/auth/pinterest/callback <— has www. so does not exactly match original url

Pinterest does not allow the configured redirect URI to send users through a second redirect. Configure the direct URL that receives the OAuth callback after the user authorizes your app.

## **2. Build and test your OAuth experience**

With Trial access enabled, implement and test the full Pinterest OAuth flow in your application.

A typical experience should follow these steps:

1. A user selects an option in your app to connect their Pinterest account
2. Your app sends the user to Pinterest to sign in and approve the requested permissions.
3. Pinterest returns the user to your configured redirect URI with an authorization code.
4. Your server securely exchanges the authorization code for an access token.
5. Your app uses that token to perform the intended Pinterest API actions.

Test this workflow from beginning to end before applying for Standard access. Pay special attention to the callback step: an incorrectly configured redirect URI is one of the most common causes of authentication failures.

Request only the permissions your app genuinely needs, and securely store access and refresh tokens. Refresh tokens should be handled before access tokens expire so users do not need to reconnect unexpectedly.

## **3. Confirm your app delivers a working Pinterest experience**

Trial access is the time to verify that your integration does what you described in your app profile.

Test the real API actions your users will rely on, such as creating or managing content, retrieving Pinterest data, or enabling a Pinterest-connected workflow in your product. Your app should demonstrate a complete, useful experience—not just a successful login.

Remember that Trial access is designed for development and testing. Content created in the testing environment may have limited visibility, and rate limits are lower than they are for production-ready Standard access.

## **4. Prepare a working demo video**

A demo video is required when requesting Standard access. The recording should show your app completing a real Pinterest API workflow from start to finish.

Your demo should include:

- The user starting the Pinterest connection from your application
- The Pinterest OAuth authentication and authorization experience
- The return to your configured redirect URI
- A successful live API action in your application
- The value the integration provides to the user

The demo does not need to be highly produced, but it should clearly show a functioning integration. A recording of a terminal or Postman workflow can be sufficient for single-user or technical use cases, as long as it demonstrates OAuth and a successful API action.

Avoid submitting slides, mockups, or a generic product tour. The goal is to show that the app is live, uses OAuth correctly, and handles Pinterest data responsibly.

## **5. Review your app profile and privacy policy**

Before requesting Standard access, review the information in your app profile.

Make sure that:

- Your app description accurately explains what the integration does.
- Your use case is clear and aligned with the functionality demonstrated in your video.
- Your privacy policy is public, accessible, and specific to your app or company.
- Your privacy policy accurately describes how Pinterest data is collected, used, stored, and protected.

Clear, consistent information helps reviewers understand your product and evaluate the request efficiently.

## **6. Submit your Standard access request**

When your integration is tested and your demo is ready, return to My apps and select Upgrade on the app you want to move to Standard access.

Review the request details, confirm your app description and privacy-policy information, upload the demo video, and submit the request.

Pinterest will review the application and send its decision by email.

## **7. Prepare for production after approval**

Once Standard access is approved, update your integration for production use.

This may include:

- Switching from sandbox credentials or endpoints to production configuration
- Using production access tokens
- Confirming the required scopes for your live use case
- Re-testing your OAuth flow and redirect URI
- Monitoring token refresh behavior and API errors

## **Standard Access Readiness Checklist**

Before submitting your request, confirm that you have:

- Received Trial access
- Configured an exact-match redirect URI
- Built and tested a complete OAuth flow
- Verified the core Pinterest API actions in your app
- Requested only necessary permissions
- Implemented secure token storage and refresh handling
- Prepared a demo showing OAuth and a live API workflow
- Updated your app description and privacy policy
- Submitted the upgrade request through My apps
